capital_gains.note: Other gains (portfolio securities) are taxable only in the residence state; the saving clause still lets the US tax its citizens, with the foreign tax credit as the relief mechanism.

employment_income.note: Salaries are taxable in the residence state unless the employment is exercised in the other state; a 183-day short-stay exemption applies when the employer is not resident in the source state and the cost is not borne by a source-state permanent establishment.

private_pensions.note: Private pensions are taxable only in the residence state, BUT the saving clause overrides this for US citizens: the US may still tax a US citizen's pension.

social_security_benefits.note: US Social Security paid to a resident of Israel is taxable only in the US; this article survives the saving clause. There is NO US-Israel totalization agreement, so self-employment social-tax double coverage is a separate, unresolved exposure.

relief.note: Double taxation is relieved primarily by credit: Israeli income tax paid is credited against US tax within the Form 1116 limitation (see foreign.py foreign_tax_credit). Claiming a treaty position may require Form 8833 disclosure.

saving_clause.rule: Each state may tax its own citizens and residents as if the treaty had not entered into force. For a US citizen living in Israel most treaty exemptions therefore do NOT apply; the surviving benefits include the relief-from-double-taxation article (foreign tax credit) and the Social Security article.

source: Convention between the United States and Israel with respect to taxes on income, signed 1975-11-20, in force 1994-12-30, Protocol signed 1993-01-26; rates cross-checked against the IRS US tax treaty table (Israel row) 2026-11-07
